The instructor's feedback asked for the problem to be shown first, so B01 is a narrated title card (project title + Riya's name + the problem) and B02 shows the problem with a real example, replacing the hesitant writer and the terms card (SQL is defined in the narration where it is first used). beats.narration_text: Ground Truth SQL. I'm Riya Kapadnis, and this is my final project pitch. The problem: AI can write database code that runs with no errors, but gives the wrong answer.

beats.narration_text: Picture an analyst asking an AI: what is our revenue by country? The AI writes SQL, the language for asking a database questions. It runs. No errors. It says the USA made four thousand six hundred sixty seven dollars. The real answer is five hundred twenty three.

beats.narration_text: Claude and I drafted that SQL to copy a common mistake, on a free sample music store database. One order from Reno, Nevada cost three ninety six, for four songs. The SQL joined the order to its songs, so the three ninety six was counted four times. Do that for every US order, and the total is almost nine times too high.

beats.narration_text: It's not the only mistake. Mix up milliseconds and seconds: three thousand five hundred long songs, not one thousand sixty nine. Count purchases, not people: eight hundred thirty five rock buyers, in a store with fifty nine customers. Link the wrong columns: no answer at all. And no errors.

beats.narration_text: Why does this happen? People ask data questions in plain English, so most never see the SQL. The AI doesn't know your data. And wrong SQL doesn't crash. It just gives a number people trust.

beats.narration_text: Other tools don't do this on your data. BIRD tests AI only on its own databases. Vanna's built-in answer test looks for words, not right numbers. On this data, it passed the answer that was nine times too high.

beats.narration_text: Ground Truth SQL fills that gap. Give it your database and questions with checked answers. It runs the AI's SQL and the checked SQL, compares the results, and gives a report card: what the AI got wrong, and why.

beats.narration_text: Where will it be used? Anywhere people ask data questions in plain English: store sales, finance, hospitals, marketing, and AI data assistants. Analysts learn what to double check. Teams test a tool before buying. Engineers see what to fix.

beats.narration_text: How does it judge? By results, not wording, since one answer can be written many ways. These two look different, but both give five hundred twenty three. On nine test queries, comparing wording judged six right. Comparing results: all nine.

beats.narration_text: It also caught a mistake in my answer key. One question asked about twenty twenty three, but the data ends in twenty thirteen. The right answer was empty, so broken SQL returning nothing looked correct. Now the tool rejects empty answers.

beats.narration_text: The problem: AI can give wrong answers that look right. Ground Truth SQL tests the AI on your own data and shows what's wrong, and why. Today the checker works; Claude's only fails were my question's fault. Next: fifty harder questions. Running SQL is easy. Being right is the test.
